title: Secretary, Department of Rural Department launches ‘National Campaign on Entrepreneurship - II’ to accelerate rural women entrepreneurship
subtitle:
‘National Campaign on Entrepreneurship- II’ launched by Secretary, Department of Rural Development aimed to push efforts towards making of 6 cr Lakhpati Didis
‘Sankalp Shakti’, the Rural Enterprise Tech Bulletin of Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana - National Rural Livelihoods Mission released by Sh. Rohit Singh, Secretary, Department of Rural Development
First edition of ‘Sankalp Shakti’ released by Secretary, Department of Rural Development. ‘Sankalp Shakti’ focusses on the empowerment of our Lakhpati Didis
body_text:
Ministry of Rural Development launched the ‘National Campaign on Entrepreneurship- II’ under the Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana–National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM) for another three months, from 21 August to 21 November 2026, with an expanded focus on both Farm, Non-Farm enterprises and marketing of SHG products.
21st August is celebrated across the world as ‘World Entrepreneurs Day’.
The campaign has been designed to promote and focus intensively on promoting rural women entrepreneurship.
Further, ‘Sankalp Shakti’, the first Rural Enterprise Technical Bulletin, was also released by the Secretary on the occasion. This Bulletin will be a monthly feature.
This focussed approach will strengthen rural women’s entrepreneurship and will contribute to the vision of making 6 crore Lakhpati Didis. The extended phase will build on the experience of the first phase and shift greater emphasis towards intensive enterprise handholding, formalisation, strengthening of producer institutions and simplification of implementation processes.
This campaign will focus on promoting entrepreneurship among SHG women across Farm and Non-Farm livelihoods, strengthening the community enterprise promotion cadre, promoting enterprise formalisation, expanding digital and e-commerce adoption, and strengthening producer groups and producer enterprises. CRP-EPs and BDSPs will be recognised as ‘Udyam Sakhis’ to provide greater visibility to the community cadre supporting enterprise promotion.
The campaign will also promote e-commerce through platforms such as ONDC, GeM and other digital platforms, besides facilitating buyer–seller meets and linkages with buyers, aggregators, retailers and institutional purchasers. States will undertake orientation of CLF leadership, exposure visits, entrepreneurship development training and support for business planning, financial literacy, product development, branding and digital marketing.
The Campaign has set ambitious outcomes, including orientation of 50,000 community cadres, entrepreneurship and livelihood training for 5 lakh SHG women, creation of a database of 5 lakh adolescent girls from SHG households, formalisation support for 50,000 enterprises, strengthening membership of Producer Groups and Producer Enterprises by 2 lakh members, promotion of agro-ecological practices among 20 lakh women, and onboarding of 25,000 SHG members on e-commerce platforms.
A key priority will be to strengthen the Farm and Non-Farm livelihood architecture by converting viable livelihood activities into sustainable women-led enterprises, rather than treating farm livelihoods only as training interventions. The campaign will complement the existing CRP-EP, EDP, SVEP and OSF architecture and support women to progress from livelihood activities to enterprise creation and growth.
The launch event was attended in person by the Secretaries/Principal Secretaries, Rural Development Departments of Bihar, Uttar Pradesh, Jammu & Kashmir, West Bengal and Goa, and virtually by the State Mission Directors/CEOs of 34 SRLMs.

enrichment.summary: The Ministry of Rural Development launched the 'National Campaign on Entrepreneurship-II' under DAY-NRLM on 21 August 2026 (World Entrepreneurs Day), running for three months to promote rural women's farm and non-farm enterprises and SHG product marketing. The campaign aims to support the goal of creating 6 crore Lakhpati Didis, with targets including training 5 lakh SHG women, formalising 50,000 enterprises, and onboarding 25,000 SHG members on e-commerce platforms. The Secretary also released the first edition of 'Sankalp Shakti', a monthly Rural Enterprise Tech Bulletin focused on Lakhpati Didi empowerment.
enrichment.context:
DAY-NRLM (Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana-National Rural Livelihoods Mission) is India's flagship rural livelihoods programme that organises rural women into Self-Help Groups (SHGs) and federates them into Village Organisations and Cluster Level Federations (CLFs), providing capital support, skill training, and market linkages. The 'Lakhpati Didi' initiative, which seeks to enable 6 crore SHG women to earn at least Rs 1 lakh annually through sustainable livelihoods, has become a flagship women's economic empowerment target frequently referenced in Budget speeches and government communications, making it a recurring current-affairs theme.

This is the second phase of an entrepreneurship campaign, building on lessons from an earlier round, and reflects a policy shift from viewing farm livelihoods merely as training exercises toward converting them into sustainable women-led enterprises. It also emphasises formalisation and digital integration through platforms like ONDC (Open Network for Digital Commerce) and GeM (Government e-Marketplace), aligning rural women entrepreneurs with India's broader digital public infrastructure and e-commerce ecosystem. The creation of a recognised community cadre ('Udyam Sakhis') indicates institutionalisation of grassroots support structures for entrepreneurship promotion.

options: Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana-National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM)
Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act
prelims_questions.explanation: The release explicitly links the National Campaign on Entrepreneurship-II and the Lakhpati Didi vision to DAY-NRLM, the rural livelihoods mission that organises women into SHGs.

prelims_questions.question: Which of the following platforms was mentioned in the release as being promoted for e-commerce adoption among rural women entrepreneurs?
prelims_questions.explanation: The release states the campaign will promote e-commerce through platforms such as ONDC, GeM, and other digital platforms.

Examine the significance of converting farm and non-farm livelihood activities into women-led enterprises for achieving inclusive rural economic growth in India.

study_notes.reason: The release names a concrete scheme (DAY-NRLM, Lakhpati Didi target, campaign specifics) that UPSC could test factually, while also illustrating a policy shift toward enterprise formalisation and digital integration that supports analytical questions on women's economic empowerment and rural livelihoods.

prelims.point: DAY-NRLM (Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana-National Rural Livelihoods Mission) is implemented by the Ministry of Rural Development and organises rural women into SHGs, Village Organisations and Cluster Level Federations (CLFs).
prelims.why_important: DAY-NRLM's institutional structure (SHG-VO-CLF) is a recurring factual detail tested in prelims on rural livelihood missions.

prelims.point: 'Lakhpati Didi' initiative aims to enable 6 crore SHG women to earn at least Rs 1 lakh annually through sustainable livelihoods.
prelims.why_important: Frequently referenced in Budget speeches, making the numerical target (6 crore) and income threshold (Rs 1 lakh) a likely objective-question detail.

prelims.point: 'National Campaign on Entrepreneurship-II' runs from 21 August to 21 November 2026, coinciding with World Entrepreneurs Day (21 August).
prelims.why_important: Dates and associated observance days are a common source of prelims distractors linking schemes to international days.

prelims.point: CRP-EPs and BDSPs under the campaign will be recognised as 'Udyam Sakhis', a community cadre supporting enterprise promotion.
prelims.why_important: New nomenclature for grassroots cadres under flagship schemes is a typical factual detail UPSC uses to test scheme-specific terminology.

prelims.point: The campaign promotes e-commerce adoption through platforms like ONDC (Open Network for Digital Commerce) and GeM (Government e-Marketplace).
prelims.why_important: ONDC and GeM are digital public infrastructure platforms frequently tested for their function and distinction from private e-commerce models.

mains.point: The campaign marks a policy shift from treating farm livelihoods as mere training interventions to converting them into sustainable women-led enterprises.
mains.theme: Women's economic empowerment through rural livelihoods
mains.analytical_use: Useful for answers on evaluating the evolution of rural livelihood missions from skill-training to enterprise-creation models.

mains.point: Emphasis on formalisation of SHG enterprises and integration with digital platforms (ONDC, GeM) reflects an attempt to mainstream rural women entrepreneurs into the formal and digital economy.
mains.theme: Digital inclusion and formalisation of rural enterprises
mains.analytical_use: Can be deployed in questions on how digital public infrastructure can be leveraged for inclusive economic growth or formalisation of the informal sector.

mains.point: Institutionalisation of a dedicated community cadre ('Udyam Sakhis') indicates a move toward building sustained grassroots support structures rather than one-off training drives.
mains.analytical_use: Supports discussion on decentralised, community-driven governance models in welfare scheme implementation.

mains.point: Ambitious quantitative targets (5 lakh women trained, 50,000 enterprises formalised, 25,000 onboarded on e-commerce) raise questions about implementation capacity and monitoring at state level.
mains.analytical_use: Useful for critically examining the gap between scheme targets and on-ground implementation feasibility.
